hourly.summary: Arsenal fans are sweating the Anfield trip like it's a dental appointment — three wins in 22 league visits, Calafiori and Rice crocked, and a referee who hasn't done a top-six game in two years. The Zubimendi soap opera rumbles on (Arteta's yo-yo selections, 'does he stay or does he go?'), while young Max Dowman's red card appeal gets laughed out of the room. Yet beneath the nail-biting, there's a stubborn refusal to accept mediocrity — 'we're one of the five best teams in Europe' they insist, even as the banter-era PTSD flares up again.

daily.summary: The day began with raw humiliation (2/10) following a shocking Carabao Cup exit to fourth-tier Fleetwood, shifted to frustrated tactical analysis with cautious optimism by midday (5/10), and settled into resigned embarrassment (4/10) by evening as fans distracted themselves with historical debates while acknowledging the women's team's dominant win as the sole positive.

weekly.summary: Arsenal fan sentiment traced a sharp V-shape across the week: starting defiant but quickly descending into anxious guardedness after a Champions League draw at Bayern and Bukayo Saka's long-term injury confirmation, before rocketing to buoyant euphoria following a routine win over Everton and simultaneous slips from title rivals. The mid-week panic over Saka's absence and transfer frustration gave way to a weekend surge of title-race belief, Ben White praise, and schadenfreude, leaving the fanbase convinced a genuine charge is underway despite the looming Anfield test.
